The SIS module for the XH component

Source: R/human-XH-SIS.R
SIS.Rd

SIS implements a family of SIS compartmental models for malaria as a system of differential equations: individuals are either susceptible \((S)\) or infected and infectious \((I)\). In its simplest form, SIS dynamics are: $$ dI/dt = h S - r I $$

This is a generalized implementation includes:

  • parameters to model treating and curing infections;

  • functions to model human demographic change;

  • functions to model mass treatment;

  • and progressive stratification

State Variables

H

the total human or host population density

I

the density of infected humans or hosts

S=H-I

the density of susceptible humans or hosts

Prevalence

x

true prevalence is \(x = I/H\)

Parameters

The parameters that are returned by get_XH_pars.SIS and also modifiable by change_XH_pars.SIS describe the dynamics, or detection by diagnostic methods.

b

the fraction of infective bites that would cause an infection

r

clearance rate for infections

c

the probability an infected person would infect a mosquito

rho or \(\rho\)

the fraction of incident infections that are treated and cured

sigma or \(\sigma\)

the rate that prevalent infections are treated and cured

q_lm

expected prevalence by light microscopy would be \(q_{lm} \;x\)

q_rdt

expected prevalence by RDT would be \(q_{rdt} \;x\)

q_pcr

expected prevalence by PCR would be \(q_{pcr} \;x\)

Dynamical Term

\(h\) or foi

The force of infection is computed and stored by Exposure as FoI

Demographic Change

Births or \(\mathbf{B}\)

the births function

Deaths or \(\mathbf{D}\)

the deaths function

NOTES:

  • The defaults are no births and no deaths

  • Use setup_births to configure Births

  • Use setup_deaths to configure Deaths

Also, see xds_info_demographic_change.

Dynamics

The model for demographic change has terms to compute births (\(\mathbf{B}\)) and deaths (\(\mathbf{D}\)): $$ dH/dt = \mathbf{B}(t,H) - \mathbf{D}(H)$$

The model for infection dynamics assumes that infections clear naturally at a constant per-capita rate \(r\). The model also includes two parameters to model treating and curing malaria infections:

  • a fraction \(\rho\) of incident infections are treated and cured;

  • in addition, prevalent infections are treated and cured at the rate \(\sigma\),

  • so the total clearance rate from treatment is \(\rho h + \sigma\) After clearing, individuals are susceptible to infection. A term for mass treatment increases the rate infections are cured: (\(\Xi(t)\)).

Infection dynamics are described by:

$$ dI/dt = h(1-\rho)(H-I) - (r + \rho h + \sigma) I - \Xi(t) I - \mathbf{D}(I) $$

The mortality function \(\mathbf{D}(I)\) computes total mortality for \(I\) using the same model as for \(H\): for example, if \(D(H)=\mu H\), then \(D(I)= \mu I.\) This model has no parameter or terms to describe disease-induced mortality.

In the compartmental model, individuals are either susceptible (\(S\)), or infected and infectious (\(I\)), so \(S=H-I.\) The equation is redundant. After solving, the orbit of the variable \(S=H-I\) is computed and attached.

Exposure

For SIS the FoI is computed (in Exposure) under the assumption that a constant fraction of infectious bites causes an infection: the parameter \(b.\)

Infectiousness

The fraction of mosquitoes that become infected after blood feeding on someone who is infectious is \(c.\) The infectious density of the human (hos) population is \(cI.\)

Mass Treatment

Mass treatment clears infections. At basic setup \(\Xi(t)=0\). To set up mass treatment, see setup_mass_treatment. Mass treatment is either:

mda(t) or \(\Xi(t)\)

mass drug administration

msat or \(\Xi(t)\)

mass screen and treat
